semantically_equivalent_models.justification: "Svc" is an abbreviation commonly used for 'Support Vector Classifier', thus they are semantically the same.

parent_models.justification: Support Vector Classifier is a specific type within the broader category of Support Vector Machines.
SVM (Support Vector Machine) is a general term that includes support vector classification as one of its types.
SVMS refers to Support Vector Machines, which includes support vector classifiers as a subset.

closest_parent_model.justification: Support Vector Machines is the direct umbrella category for Support Vector Classifiers, making it the closest in hierarchy.

child_models.justification: It is looking to identify a more specific type or extension of Support Vector Classifier, however it may have no closer child as per the list.

closest_child_model.justification: As per the list, no more specific subclass or variant is provided that fits as a closer child model directly under support vector classifier.

sibling_models.justification: SVM with Linear Kernel is another type of SVM and hence a sibling to Support Vector Classifier.
One-Class SVM, like Support Vector Classifier, is another subclass under the Support Vector Machines umbrella.
GS-SVM is another specialized SVM variant, placing it as a sibling to Support Vector Classifier.
Support Vector Regression (SVR) is another application of Support Vector Machines, equal in hierarchy to support vector classifier.

closest_sibling_model.justification: SVM with Linear Kernel is very similar to Support Vector Classifier, both being specific implementations within support vector machines with tailored functions.
